# Project Room (dsh-project-room)
English | 中文
One project = one persistent group chat. The user, the coordinator agent, frontend, backend, testing
and ops all talk on the same group-message timeline, while each of them has a **genuinely independe
nt** Harness session, its own working context and real execution capability.
This is not a chat-UI skin: every delivery in the room lands in a real session, task state is driven
only by real execution and evidence, and models are routed per member.
## 1. Install and enable
The plugin is a pure ESM package with **no installed dependencies**: the host half imports only Node
built-ins, and the browser half is a self-registering classic script. No build toolchain and no ext
ra package in the profile is needed.

### 4.3 The user changes a requirement directly
An explicit instruction such as `@frontend change this entry point to SMS verification.` goes throug
h the full path: save the original words → bind the target task → write a new requirement decision r
evision (a human requirement is adopted directly) → mark the deterministically affected tasks as `ne
edsSync` → notify the relevant members → require each to report its sync state. **Passing results fr
om an old revision cannot be reused**; they must be re-verified against the new revision.
"@frontend why is it designed this way?" is a question and does not turn into a code task by itself.
## 5. What you can see in the room
- **Panel**: the top bar has the project title, status, project switcher and task/member entries. Wi
de screens show three columns — "Project room / Timeline / Tasks and models"; when space is short th
e side columns collapse into drawers instead of squeezing the chat into a strip. The `Aa` control in

the top-right offers **standard / large / extra-large** text sizes, stored on this machine.
- **Tim
eline**: separated by day; your own messages sit in bubbles on the right, member messages on the lef
t. Fenced code renders as code blocks, and inline code, bold text and delivered mentions have explic

it styles; hover a message to reply, or `@` the other side in the input box.
- **Input area**: a fro
sted-glass input card; the `@` popup supports keyboard selection, and the quote bar, recipient chips

and the "how many AI members will be reached" hint are all visible before sending.
- **Member colum
n**: the avatar menu offers `@ them`, view member, view/switch model, view current task, pause and l
eave; status dots and model provenance (member-pinned / role default / project default / allowed poo

l) are visible inline.
- **Tasks and models**: the same column has two tabs, "Tasks / Models". The T
asks page shows acceptance progress, task cards (status, revision, owner, acceptance criteria, depen
dency wait, artifact verification state), project decisions and sync receipts, deliveries and recove

ry; the Models page shows project defaults, role defaults, selection mode and the allowed pool.

## 8. Known limitations
Only the most important ones to know first:
- **File and command tools for member sessions come from `memberAgentPreset`**: without it, members
only have room-collaboration tools. The preset is a **two-part contract** — `meta.agentPreset` only
writes the session header, and the real tool tree is mounted onto the member context by `agentPreset
s.mount()`; the plugin does both (both create and resume), and **both paths have been verified in th

e real host**: members really ran `node --version`, really wrote files, and passed acceptance.
- **L
ifecycle operations never pretend a member has stopped**: archive/recycle-bin blocks new execution f
irst, then requests stop and **re-reads the real agent state**; only a confirmed stop enters the tar
get state, otherwise it stays at "stop unconfirmed" (`BLOCKED`). Verified on the real desktop app: w
hile the stop request was in flight `confirmed=false`, and only after reconciliation succeeded was t

he project archived.
- **Project lifecycle is a soft-delete loop, not "dropping the database"**: mov
ing to the recycle bin only changes the project state and keeps all plugin data; permanent deletion
only clears the project's plugin-private records, the resource-ownership ledger and plugin-owned ses
sions, and **never deletes source code, user workspaces, borrowed sessions, worktrees or host logs b
y default**. External copies the plugin cannot prove cleaned are honestly kept and reported. Recycle
-bin expiry only shows a date hint and **never auto-purges**. A partial resource release enters "cle

anup blocked" (`PURGE_BLOCKED`), keeps the data and allows an idempotent retry.
- **Optional source
/ temp-file / worktree cleanup is not implemented**: the advanced cleanup in the spec needs a separa
te dangerous operation, per-path authorization, ownership verification and a host deletion receipt;
this version does not provide it, and the cleanup preview explicitly lists the source code, worktree
s and host logs that are kept. Any "clean the source code" action must not be treated as supported.
